stem_md: Which is the best way to dispense liquids using a volumetric pipet?

options.label: A
options.text_md: The pipet is immersed in the liquid to be dispensed, then lifted with a gloved finger on the top and the liquid allowed to drain to the mark. The remaining contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container.

options.label: B
options.text_md: The pipet is immersed in the liquid to be dispensed, then lifted with a gloved finger on the top and the liquid allowed to drain to the mark. The remaining contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container, with a pipet bulb used to gently blow out any residual droplets.

options.label: C
options.text_md: The tip of the pipet is submerged below the surface of the liquid and suction is applied using a pipet bulb until the liquid rises above the level of the mark. A gloved finger is then applied to the top of the pipet and the liquid allowed to drain to the mark. The remaining contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container.

options.label: D
options.text_md: The tip of the pipet is submerged below the surface of the liquid and suction is applied by mouth until the liquid rises to the level of the mark. The contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container.

stem_md:
Tert-butyl alcohol reacts with aqueous hydrochloric acid to give tert-butyl chloride.

$\ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + H+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq) + H2O(l)}$

For this reaction, Rate = $k[\ce{(CH3)3COH}][\ce{H+}]$. With which mechanism is this rate law consistent?

options.label: B
options.text_md:
$\ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + H+(aq) <=> (CH3)3C(OH2)+(aq)}$ fast

$\ce{(CH3)3C(OH2)+(aq) -> (CH3)3C+(aq) + H2O(l)}$ slow

$\ce{(CH3)3C+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq)}$ fast

options.label: C
options.text_md:
$\ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq) + OH-(aq)}$ slow

$\ce{OH-(aq) + H+(aq) -> H2O(l)}$ fast

options.label: D
options.text_md:
$\ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) -> (CH3)3C+(aq) + OH-(aq)}$ slow

$\ce{(CH3)3C+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq)}$ fast

$\ce{OH-(aq) + H+(aq) -> H2O(l)}$ fast
